mentl/9b02764:
Yesterday's Hβ.infer.mixed-positional-labeled-call is retracted the day
after it was named. Six shapes measured clean — all-labeled, mixed,
all-positional, SYNTAX's own three-param example, defaulted trailing,
label-skips-over. The mixed form has never been broken. The original probe
wrote `fn spawn(...)` and the diagnostic was true about a different spawn.

What it was actually seeing: a user program declaring a function whose name
is an op of a linked effect gets no diagnostic. The declaration is
unreachable — the call performs the op — and the body is judged against the
op's signature, so the only sign is a type error naming a shape the author
never wrote. Coverage elsewhere is correct and was mapped: map, fold, len,
byte_at, str_slice, report and hash all raise the armed E_DuplicateFnName;
eprint_string, mint and intern_str are not in a user link at all. spawn is
the one that is linked and silent, because it is an op and the duplicate-fn
check correctly does not cover ops.

Two builds went in before the probe and both were reverted whole: a
six-arm class with an env read at pre_register_stmt, then the same read by
kind. Both marched clean with census 0 and neither fired. The probe ended
it — env_lookup returns NOT FOUND for every name at that phase, 225 of 225
on one micro. The env is not readable there, and the walk's own comment
says so for its own reason. No site is known to work yet; the next probe is
named with what it decides.
mentl/9bc0b00:
No write to src/**.mn or lib/**.mn until a medium verb has named that path
this session. check, audit, query, tighten, a cursor address — any of them,
and one that answers with errors still counts, because the requirement is
that the question was put and demanding a clean answer would deadlock a
mid-refactor file.

The pre-edit hook's own header read "never blocks — audit is POST-edit". It
printed the eight interrogations and I read past them for ten iterations,
editing wheel files without once asking mentl audit what it already knew.
When I finally ran it, it answered in one command what hand-reading had not,
and mentl tighten exposed a fabricating verb nobody had exercised. PLAN §0's
argument about prose applies to the scaffold that was supposed to enforce it.

The pre-bash hook records the consult at the exact branch where it already
decides a command IS a medium verb, so the ledger costs nothing and cannot be
bypassed by phrasing. A session starts with it empty: what the medium said
last session is about a tree that has since moved.

Priced before imposed. mentl check costs 0.65s/208MB on types.mn,
0.73s/227MB on lexer.mn, 2.53s/725MB on infer.mn — once per file per session,
not per edit. Running the audit itself at the edit stays refused at
4.91s/777MB and image-gated.

Falsified five ways through the hooks' own stdin contract: an unconsulted
wheel edit exits 2, a consult writes the marker, the same edit then exits 0, a
different wheel file stays refused, and a cursor address counts. The first
attempt failed and the failure was the find — the ledger sat below the hook's
mentl-led early exit and never ran, so it moved to that branch.

Scope is wheel source. tests/, docs and the seed keep the reminder alone; the
law is about editing the medium without asking it.

No wheel change, so no march; the pin is unmoved at 567a96659693.
mentl/9b05c76:
The march verb compiles the wheel in-process through the canonical
converged stdin chain, streams the emission through the new
wat_to_file(fd) sink into .build/march/m2.wat, reads the census inside
the same install, and verdicts against the last generation. Its first
CLEAN was against the bash march's own m2, so the in-process and exec
invocation routes are proven byte-identical; the re-run is CLEAN
against itself. The walk skips fd_readdir's self and parent links —
the unfiltered walk descended src/./. forever, two bytes a level,
until the alloc ceiling.

wat_to_file is the third emission sink: write-through to an fd opened
by fs_create_impl (path_open write+create+trunc returning the fd), so
bytes reach the host at each arm and the emit phase's per-fn region
resets cannot touch the product. The scope law written at
wat_to_string's decl names the inverse: the collecting sink is per-fn
only, because a whole-compile install banks segment pointers the
region resets zero. That was the in-process battery's silent break
since the emit-arena landed — its verb gate never re-ran while the
board's micros went through the bash loop. mentl test streams
per-micro wat through the same sink now: 114/114 in-process.

flat_fill_concat drains an explicit heap stack of (node, offset)
pairs — call depth is representation alternation, never concat depth;
the recursive form died at fold-built line depth and the drain is
proven on a 5000-deep rope. The float family goes DAG-honest:
callee-first order plus Float pins on parse_float, parse_float_body,
and parse_mantissa_f64, because the single-pass DAG judgment floored
loose forward schemes' f64 results to words — an assembly refusal in
mentl run.

mentl/9bcfe4a:
Effect operations as first-class values:
- compile_var_load now wraps bare effect op references in closure wrappers
- map(resolve, xs) works: resolve becomes |x| perform resolve(x)
- Only activates inside function scopes (scope_depth > 0) to avoid
  shadowing user globals like 'result'

This was THE blocker for the self-hosted type checker. The prelude's
handler-based map/filter/fold call f(elem) inside yield handlers —
when f was an effect op passed as a bare value, it resolved to Unit
because effect ops were never stored as globals.

Validated and frozen (chattr +i):

  Layer 1: eff.lux, ty.lux (effect algebra, type representation)
  Layer 2: infer.lux, check.lux (type rules, checker engine)
  Layer 3: lexer.lux, parser.lux (frontend with |> <| <> support)
  Layer 3: suggest.lux, display.lux (diagnostics, type display)

9 frozen files. The entire self-hosted compiler architecture.

Cycle 3a's clear_stains_on_round_reset cleared the stain set every
round transition, keeping the visual scope tight. The brand-defining
synthesis primitive (VISUAL_TARGET_PACK.md) is stronger when the
arena accumulates ALL of a match's violence — by round 5 of a BO5

Renamed clear_stains_on_round_reset -> clear_stains_on_match_reset.
Trigger condition flipped from "transition into Countdown from
non-Countdown" to "transition out of MatchOver". MatchOver is
currently terminal in sim, so within a single app session stains

state will all accumulate together across rounds, making the arena
state telegraph match progression at a glance — both for live
players and for replay viewers scrubbing through the match.
noodles/9bc6624:
The pie was pushed discrete per-16th values that a CSS transition then
interpolated between — a second clock (the browser's animation timeline)
that only stayed honest if every event landed on its frame. Under a
janky frame it stalled at the step value, then jumped and re-swept.

Drive it directly instead. The audio side emits a per-track loop anchor
(the AudioContext time of the current cycle's step 0, and the cycle
duration); a per-frame pump reads the position being heard right now
(audio.heardNow = context time minus output latency) and sets each
playing clip's pie to exactly (now - start) / dur. The pie is now a pure
function of playback position, re-derived every frame — no second clock,
no dependence on an event arriving this frame, so it cannot drift.

Verified over real playback at 120 BPM: the 1-bar pie wraps at 2000,
2017, 1983, 2000ms (wall) and 2024, 1992, 1984, 2000ms (audio) — dead on
2000ms, within one 17ms display frame, and it updates continuously every
frame instead of chunking. Removes the now-dead --pct transition,
pie-snap, and applyStepDur/--stepdur.

Two irreducible residuals remain, both fundamental: one display frame of
granularity (can't paint faster than refresh), and the platform's
output-latency estimate that heardNow leans on (imperfect over
Bluetooth). Everything a visual can control is now locked to the clock.
